trigger: The T_* log lines are written synchronously on the Spark consumer and convergence threads, the send workers and (T_server) the ingest thread, so a blocked log sink stalls whichever thread is writing; comments claimed delivery never depends on log-sink health. unhappy-path derived HIGH via I5(b); cpp-safety derived MEDIUM.
summary: The T_* log lines are written synchronously on the Spark consumer and convergence threads, the send workers and (T_server) the ingest thread, so a blocked log sink stalls whichever thread is writing; comments claimed delivery never depends on log-sink health. unhappy-path derived HIGH via I5(b); cpp-safety derived MEDIUM. Also reported by: cpp-safety.

Comments corrected to describe the real extent of the decoupling (d00a1bc64, 0b51597c2); the exposure is recorded as a named flip precondition in docs/spark-flip-gate.md section 7 (bc7b242ec), tied to #4606 closing. Adjudicated ACCEPT-WITH-PRECONDITION: no decoupling before this merge, because it would not remove the live exposure (every spdlog sink is synchronous and process-wide) and the Spark-side tolerance is by design (ADR-0021 Decision 3).
adjudication_rationale: Independent adjudication (not the reporter, not the author). LIVE legacy path (T_wire on the guard worker, T_server on the ingest thread): I5 with E5, I5(b) does not apply (per-guard and per-stream threads, not a serialised path shared across security operations, and the line follows the operation it describes), derived MEDIUM, and mostly pre-existing coupling because guard workers already log synchronously. DORMANT Spark path (T_detect and Spark-path T_wire): E6 does not apply (unreachability is a constructor default, not a proof) and E4 does not apply, but the preamble scores dormant code on the I6 axis, so MEDIUM for this diff; a flip PR still carrying synchronous writes derives HIGH and is BLOCKING. The remediation (truthful comments, a named F14 precondition covering the convergence lanes and T_server, the retirement plan) is adequate to merge; decoupling now would cost roughly 150-250 lines of new thread infrastructure without removing the live exposure.
